prompt:
A native embedded device screen in portrait 3:4 (240x320 TFT), shown flat and edge to edge with crisp readable text, no device body, hands or desk around it. It is the startup screen of BayuPandu, an open-source paragliding variometer, shown for about three seconds when the pilot switches the instrument on at launch, while it checks its sensors. The reference image is a real BayuPandu screen: carry over its green highway-sign panel with white border and rounded corners on a near-black surround, white heavy Overpass road-sign lettering in capitals, and flat polygon sign arrows; do not copy its flight numbers or layout. No yellow anywhere: yellow is reserved for warnings and nothing is wrong here.

What leads: the BayuPandu mark, large and centred in the upper half: a highway route-marker shield outlined in white, holding one bold sign arrow that rises and bends like air lifting in a thermal (the name means "wind guide"). Under the shield, the wordmark BAYUPANDU in road-sign capitals, and small beneath it V0.1.0.

Below a white rule, the self-test set as a route assembly of four short lines, each a small white sign arrow, a legend and a result: BARO OK, GPS 7 SAT, LOG READY, BATT 92%. The last line is still checking. A small caption at the very bottom: ANY BUTTON TO SKIP.
